q24617.en: Licence suspension is an additional penalty that comes from breaking certain articles of the Highway Code.

explain.short: Suspension never comes alone: it is added to the fine for some serious offences listed in the Highway Code.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'sanzione accessoria' means an extra penalty added on top of the fine.

sceneParams.caption: Suspension: an extra penalty for some offences

q24618.en: Licence suspension is ordered, for example, when a new driver drives without respecting the limits on vehicles and speeds.

explain.short: A new driver (neopatentato) has extra limits on vehicle power and speed. Breaking them is serious: fine plus suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'neopatentato' means a driver who got the licence recently; the limits are only for them.

sceneParams.caption: New driver breaks the limits: suspension
lines: New driver: first years of licence B
Too powerful car or too fast

q24620.en: Licence suspension is ordered when you exceed the maximum speed limits by more than 40 km/h.

explain.short: Going more than 40 km/h over the limit is very dangerous. The law adds a suspension to the fine.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'di oltre 40 km/h' (by more than 40 km/h): this is the speed that brings suspension, not a small excess.

sceneParams.caption: Over 40 km/h above the limit: suspension

q24621.en: Licence suspension may be ordered when you drive, on a motorway, in the emergency lane in cases not allowed by the Highway Code.

explain.short: The emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) is only for breakdowns and emergencies. Driving in it without a reason is serious and can bring suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'in casi non previsti' (in cases not allowed): stopping there for a breakdown is fine, driving along it is not.

sceneParams.caption: Emergency lane is not a driving lane
lines: Driving in it without a reason

q24622.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver drives under the effect of drugs.

explain.short: Drugs slow your reactions and change what you see. Drug driving is a crime and the licence is suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'sostanze stupefacenti' means drugs.

q24623.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver drives while drunk.

explain.short: Driving with too much alcohol in the blood (stato di ebbrezza) is a serious offence. The licence is suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'stato di ebbrezza alcolica' means drunk, over the alcohol limit.

q24624.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver refuses to take the tests for possible drunkenness.

explain.short: If you refuse the alcohol test, the law treats you like a drunk driver. So the licence is suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'rifiuta di sottoporsi' (refuses to take): refusing is not a way to escape the penalty.

sceneParams.caption: Refusing the alcohol test: suspension
lines: Police ask for an alcohol test

q24625.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver runs away without helping the person they hit.

explain.short: After an accident you must stop and help the injured person. Running away is very serious: the licence is suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'fugge senza prestare soccorso' means runs away without giving help.

q24626.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver illegally drives a vehicle that has been seized.

explain.short: A seized vehicle (sotto sequestro) must not be used. Driving it anyway is serious and brings suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'sottoposto a sequestro' means seized by the authorities; 'abusivamente' means without permission.

q24627.en: Licence suspension may be ordered against anyone who has forged or counterfeited the vehicle insurance documents.

explain.short: Fake insurance papers are a serious fraud. Besides the other penalties, the licence can be suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'falsificato o contraffatto' means faked or forged.

q24628.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver drives with a suspended licence.

explain.short: If you drive while your licence is already suspended, the penalty is harder: revocation (revoca), not another suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'con patente sospesa': the licence is already suspended, so the next step is 'revoca'.

sceneParams.caption: Driving while suspended: revocation, not suspension

q24629.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the licence holder permanently loses the physical requirements.

explain.short: If the physical requirements are lost for ever, the licence is revoked (revoca). Suspension is only for a period of time.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'definitivamente' (permanently): for ever means revocation, not suspension.

sceneParams.caption: Fitness lost for ever: revocation
lines: For ever, not for a time

q24630.en: Licence suspension is ordered when doubts arise about whether the required requirements still exist.

explain.short: When there are doubts about a driver's fitness, the licence is checked again (revisione): a new medical check or exam. It is not suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'dubbi' (doubts) lead to 'revisione' (a new check), not to suspension.

q24631.en: Licence suspension is ordered at the same time as the notice that the points have reached zero.

explain.short: With zero points the driver must take the exam again (revisione). The licence is not suspended.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'azzeramento dei punti' (points at zero) means a new exam, not suspension.

sceneParams.caption: Zero points: new exam, not suspension

q24632.en: Licence suspension may be ordered when you exceed the maximum speed limits by 20 km/h.

explain.short: Going 20 km/h over the limit costs a fine and points. Suspension starts when you go more than 40 km/h over.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'di 20 km/h': too small; suspension is for 'oltre 40 km/h'.

sceneParams.caption: +20 km/h: fine and points, no suspension

q24632.reviewNote: Legge 177/2024 may add a short suspension for repeated 10-40 km/h speeding in towns; check the official FALSE still fits.

q24633.en: Licence suspension may be ordered when you drive without having your driving licence with you.

explain.short: If you have a valid licence but left it at home, you only pay a fine and must show it later. No suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'senza avere con sè' (without having it with you): you have a licence, you just forgot it.

sceneParams.caption: Licence left at home: only a fine

q24634.en: Licence suspension is ordered when you drive with an unreadable or damaged licence.

explain.short: A worn or damaged licence must be replaced with a duplicate. You get a fine, not a suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'illeggibile o deteriorata' (unreadable or damaged): ask for a duplicate, no suspension.

q24635.en: Licence suspension is ordered when, on request of the police, you cannot show the warning triangle.

explain.short: Not having the warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) costs a fine. It does not suspend the licence.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'segnale mobile di pericolo' is the warning triangle: a small fault, only a fine.

sceneParams.caption: No warning triangle: only a fine

q24636.en: Licence suspension is ordered when the holder no longer has the moral requirements.

explain.short: Losing the moral requirements (requisiti morali), for example after certain crimes, leads to revocation (revoca), not suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'requisiti morali': losing them means 'revoca'.

q24637.en: Licence suspension is ordered when you leave the vehicle parked in the spaces reserved for disabled people.

explain.short: Parking in a disabled space without the permit is wrong and costs a fine (and the car can be towed). It does not suspend the licence.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'spazi destinati ai disabili': a parking offence, no suspension.

sceneParams.caption: Disabled space: fine, no suspension
lines: Car parked in a disabled space

q24638.en: Licence suspension is ordered when you have not paid the car tax on time.

explain.short: The car tax (bollo) is a tax on owning the car. Paying it late brings extra charges, never a licence suspension.
explain.rule: Suspension (sospensione) is an extra penalty added to the fine for serious offences, such as speeding by more than 40 km/h, alcohol, drugs or hit-and-run. Driving while suspended or losing the requirements leads to revocation (revoca); doubts lead to a new check (revisione); small faults cost only a fine.
explain.trap: 'bollo dell'auto' is a tax, not a driving offence.

q24639.en: Every driving licence starts with 20 points.

explain.short: When you get your licence, it has 20 points. Offences take points away from these 20.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: '20 punti': the starting number; other numbers in the quiz are wrong.

q24640.en: The points on the licence go down when you commit particular offences against the Highway Code.

explain.short: Only some offences, chosen by the law, take points away. They are the ones that put road safety at risk.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'particolari infrazioni' (particular offences): not every offence, only some.

q24641.en: When the driver has used up all the points on the licence, they must undergo a review of it.

explain.short: With zero points you must prove again that you can drive: you take the theory and driving exams again (revisione).
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'revisione' means a new exam; the licence is not taken away for ever.

sceneParams.caption: Zero points: take the exam again

q24643.en: Offences that cost points, committed in the first three years after getting a category B licence, are punished with double the points.

explain.short: New drivers have less experience, so in the first 3 years of licence B every points offence costs twice as many points.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'doppio' (double): not triple.

q24644.en: If you commit several offences at the same time that cost points, at most 15 points can be taken off, unless the offences lead to suspension of the licence.

explain.short: The law sets a ceiling: several offences in one go cost at most 15 points. The ceiling does not apply if an offence brings suspension.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'al massimo 15 punti' and 'salvo che... sospensione': both details must be right.

sceneParams.caption: Several offences at once: max 15 points

q24645.en: If for two years the driver commits no offences that cost points, a driver with fewer than 20 points gets all 20 points back.

explain.short: Good behaviour is rewarded: two years without losing points bring the score back to 20.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'tutti i 20 punti': back to 20, not to 30.

sceneParams.caption: Two clean years: back to 20 points
lines: Two years with no points lost

q24647.en: Every driving licence starts with 30 points.

explain.short: The starting amount is 20 points, not 30.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: '30 punti': wrong number; the start is 20.

q24648.en: The points on the licence go down when you commit any offence against the Highway Code.

explain.short: Not every offence costs points. Only specific offences, listed by the law, take points away.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'una qualunque infrazione' (any offence): too broad, only some do.

q24649.en: The points on the licence go down only when you commit an offence that leads to suspension or withdrawal of the licence.

explain.short: Many offences cost points without any suspension, for example using the phone while driving. So 'only' is wrong.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'esclusivamente' (only): points are lost also for offences without suspension.

q24650.en: Offences that cost points, committed in the first three years after getting your first licence, are punished with triple the points.

explain.short: For new drivers the points are doubled, not tripled.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'triplo' (triple): wrong, the rule is 'doppio' (double).

q24651.en: Attending a special course and passing a specific exam allow the holder of licence A or B to get back 9 points, up to a maximum of 30 points.

explain.short: For licence A or B the course gives back 6 points, not 9. The course does not take you up to 30 points.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: '9 punti' and '30 punti': wrong numbers.

sceneParams.caption: Course for A/B: 6 points back, not 9
lines: Licence A or B: 6 points back

q24652.en: If you commit several offences at the same time that cost points, at most 10 points can be taken off, unless the offences lead to revocation of the licence.

explain.short: The ceiling for several offences at once is 15 points, not 10.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'al massimo 10 punti': wrong number; the ceiling is 15.

sceneParams.caption: Max at once is 15 points, not 10

q24653.en: If for two years the driver commits no offences that cost points, a driver with fewer than 20 points gets 30 points.

explain.short: Two clean years bring a driver back to 20 points, not 30. Extra bonus points above 20 come only later, for drivers who already have 20.
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'entra in possesso di 30 punti': wrong, they get back to 20.

sceneParams.caption: Two clean years: back to 20, not 30
lines: Two years with no points lost

q24654.en: When the driver has used up all the points on the licence, the licence is revoked.

explain.short: Zero points do not mean revocation. The driver must take the exam again (revisione).
explain.rule: Every licence starts with 20 points. Only some offences take points away; new drivers (first 3 years of licence B) lose double. At most 15 points at once, unless there is suspension or revocation. Two years without losing points bring you back to 20. Zero points: new exam (revisione).
explain.trap: 'revocata' (revoked): wrong, zero points mean 'revisione'.

sceneParams.caption: Zero points: new exam, not revocation

q24655.en: Exceeding the speed limits by more than 10 km/h while driving costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Speeding is dangerous. Going more than 10 km/h over the limit costs a fine and points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'di oltre 10 km/h': above 10 km/h over the limit, points are lost.

sceneParams.caption: Over 10 km/h above the limit: points lost

q24656.en: Not respecting some rules on overtaking costs points on the licence.

explain.short: A wrong overtake can cause a head-on crash. Many overtaking faults cost points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'alcune norme' (some rules): not all, but many overtaking faults cost points.

q24657.en: Using a mobile phone without an earpiece or hands-free while driving costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Holding the phone takes your hands and eyes off the road. It costs a fine and points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'senza auricolare o viva voce': with these devices it is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Phone in hand while driving: points lost

q24658.en: Riding without a helmet when it is required, or with the helmet badly fastened, costs points on the licence.

explain.short: The helmet protects the head only if it is worn and fastened. Without it, you lose points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'mal allacciato' (badly fastened) counts as no helmet.

sceneParams.caption: No helmet or not fastened: points lost

q24659.en: Not keeping a safe distance, when this has caused an accident, costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Too short a distance leads to rear-end crashes. If a crash happens, you lose points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'da cui sia derivato un incidente' (that caused an accident): the crash is the condition here.

sceneParams.caption: Too close and a crash: points lost

q24660.en: Not using lights, or using them wrongly, while driving costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Lights let you see and be seen. Not using them, or dazzling others, costs points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'mancato utilizzo o l'uso improprio': both no lights and wrong lights.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong use of lights: points lost
lines: Night: lights off, or high beam
Others cannot see or are dazzled

q24661.en: Carrying too much load or too many people while driving costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Too much weight or too many people make braking and steering worse. It costs points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'sovraccarico' is too much load; 'sovrannumero' is too many people.

sceneParams.caption: Overload or too many people: points lost

q24662.en: Not wearing glasses or lenses while driving, if they are prescribed, costs points on the licence.

explain.short: If your licence says you need glasses or contact lenses, you must wear them. Without them, you lose points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'se prescritte' (if prescribed): only for drivers whose licence requires them.

sceneParams.caption: Prescribed glasses not worn: points lost

q24663.en: Driving in the emergency lane on a motorway, outside the allowed cases, costs points on the licence.

explain.short: The emergency lane is only for breakdowns and emergency vehicles. Driving in it costs points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'al di fuori dei casi previsti': stopping for a breakdown is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Emergency lane: points lost
lines: Driving in it without a reason

q24664.en: Driving under the effect of drugs costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Drug driving is very dangerous. Besides suspension, it costs many points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'sostanze stupefacenti' means drugs.

q24665.en: Racing on private tracks, being under 24 and having only licence B, costs points on the licence.

explain.short: A private track is not a public road, so the Highway Code points do not apply there. Age and licence do not change this.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'piste private' (private tracks): not a road, so no points.

q24666.en: Leaving the car parked in front of a driveway costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Blocking a driveway (passo carrabile) is a parking offence: fine and possibly towing, but no points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'passo carrabile' (driveway): a parking fault, only a fine.

q24668.en: Driving without having with you the registration document of the vehicle you are driving costs points on the licence.

explain.short: You must carry the registration document (carta di circolazione). If you forget it, you pay a fine and show it later, but you lose no points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'senza avere con sé': a forgotten document is only a fine.

sceneParams.caption: Document left at home: only a fine

q24669.en: Driving without having with you the certificate of ownership of the vehicle you are driving costs points on the licence.

explain.short: The certificate of ownership (certificato di proprietà) does not have to be carried while driving. So no points are lost.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'certificato di proprietà' is not one of the documents to carry.

sceneParams.caption: Ownership certificate: not needed on board

q24670.en: Driving a vehicle owned by someone else without authorisation from the Motorizzazione Civile costs points on the licence.

explain.short: You can drive a friend's car with the owner's permission. No authorisation from the Motorizzazione Civile (transport office) is needed, and no points are lost.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'autorizzazione della Motorizzazione Civile': it does not exist for this.

sceneParams.caption: Someone else's car: no office permit needed

q24671.en: The points lost for a Highway Code offence are doubled if it is committed riding a motorcycle with more than 35 kW of power.

explain.short: Points are doubled only for new drivers, never because of the vehicle's power.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'raddoppiata... potenza superiore a 35 kW': power does not double points.

q24672.en: The points lost for a Highway Code offence are doubled if it is committed driving a car with more than 115 kW of power.

explain.short: Points are doubled only for new drivers, never because of the car's power.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'raddoppiata... potenza superiore a 115 kW': power does not double points.

q24673.en: Driving a car with eight seats including the driver, with a category C licence, costs points on the licence.

explain.short: A car with up to 9 seats including the driver can be driven with licence B, and a C holder also has B. So it is allowed and no points are lost.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'otto posti compreso il conducente': still a normal car for licence B.

q24674.en: Driving a car on a motorway or main extra-urban road when you got licence B less than six months ago costs points on the licence.

explain.short: There is no ban on motorways for new drivers. They must respect lower speed limits, but driving there is allowed.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'da meno di sei mesi': no rule forbids new drivers from motorways.

sceneParams.caption: New driver on the motorway: allowed

q24675.en: Driving, on a public holiday, a loaded lorry with a maximum laden mass of less than 3.5 tonnes costs points on the licence.

explain.short: The holiday driving ban is for heavy goods vehicles, not for small lorries under 3.5 tonnes. So it is allowed and no points are lost.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'inferiore a 3,5 tonnellate': a light lorry, the holiday ban does not apply.

sceneParams.caption: Light lorry on a holiday: allowed

q24676.en: Driving a vehicle that has not had its required periodic inspection costs points on the licence.

explain.short: Missing the periodic inspection (revisione periodica) is an offence about the vehicle: fine, and the vehicle cannot be used until checked. No points.
explain.rule: Points are lost for offences that are dangerous while driving (speed, overtaking, phone, helmet, distance, lights, overload, glasses, emergency lane, drugs). Paperwork and parking faults cost only a fine. Double points are only for new drivers.
explain.trap: 'revisione periodica' is the vehicle's check: a fine, not points.

sceneParams.caption: Vehicle check missed: fine, no points

q24677.en: The driving licence is confirmed if the holder still has the required physical and mental requirements.

explain.short: Renewing the licence means checking that you are still fit to drive: body and mind.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'requisiti fisici e psichici' (physical and mental requirements): the only thing checked.

sceneParams.caption: Still fit to drive: licence confirmed

q24678.en: The driving licence is confirmed after a positive result of the special medical check done by an authorised doctor.

explain.short: To renew, you visit an authorised doctor. If the check is positive, the licence is confirmed.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'medico autorizzato' (authorised doctor): not any doctor, one authorised for this.

q24679.en: The driving licence is confirmed by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport after a check of physical and mental fitness done by an authorised doctor.

explain.short: The doctor checks your fitness, then the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport confirms the licence and sends the new one.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'Ministero delle infrastrutture e dei trasporti': the Ministry confirms, not the Prefetto.

sceneParams.caption: Ministry confirms after the medical check

keywords.it: Ministero delle infrastrutture e dei trasporti

q24680.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years if issued or confirmed to someone who is not over 50.

explain.short: Under 50 you are usually fit and healthy, so licence B lasts 10 years.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'dieci anni... non ha superato i 50 anni': 10 years only under 50.

q24681.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for five years if issued or confirmed to someone aged between 50 and 70.

explain.short: From 50 to 70 health is checked more often, so licence B lasts 5 years.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'cinque anni... fra i 50 e i 70 anni': 5 years in this age range.

q24682.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for three years if issued or confirmed to someone aged between 70 and 80.

explain.short: From 70 to 80 the checks are more frequent: licence B lasts 3 years.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'tre anni... fra i 70 e gli 80 anni': 3 years in this age range.

q24683.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for two years if issued or confirmed to someone over 80.

explain.short: Over 80 you can still drive, but the licence lasts only 2 years, so health is checked often.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'due anni... superato gli 80 anni': over 80 it is still renewed, every 2 years.

q24684.en: A category BE licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years if issued or confirmed to someone who is not over 50.

explain.short: BE (car with a heavier trailer) follows the same periods as B: 10 years under 50.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'categoria BE': same validity as B.

q24685.en: A category A licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years if issued or confirmed to someone who is not over 50.

explain.short: The motorbike licence A follows the same periods as B: 10 years under 50.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'categoria A': same validity as B.

q24686.en: A category B SPECIAL (BS) licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for five years if issued or confirmed to someone who is not over 70.

explain.short: B speciale is for drivers with a physical disability and an adapted car. It lasts 5 years up to 70.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'B SPECIALE (BS)': shorter validity, 5 years up to 70.

sceneParams.caption: Licence BS up to 70: valid 5 years

q24687.en: A category B licence is confirmed by the Prefetto after a visit checking the moral requirements.

explain.short: The licence is confirmed by the Ministry after a MEDICAL check of physical and mental fitness. The Prefetto and moral requirements have nothing to do with renewal.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'Prefetto' and 'requisiti morali': both wrong for renewal.

sceneParams.caption: Renewal: Ministry and doctor, not Prefetto

q24688.en: With an expired driving licence you can still keep driving for at most three days.

explain.short: There is no grace period. When the licence has expired, you must not drive at all until it is renewed.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'per un tempo massimo di tre giorni': no grace days exist.

sceneParams.caption: Expired licence: no driving, not even 3 days

q24689.en: The driving licence is confirmed after passing a periodic technical driving test (driving exam).

explain.short: Renewal needs only a medical check. You do not take the driving exam again.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'prova tecnica di guida (esame di guida) periodica': no repeated driving exam.

sceneParams.caption: Renewal: medical check, no driving exam

q24690.en: A holder allowed to drive vehicles of category A and category B must take two separate medical visits, one for each category, to confirm the licence.

explain.short: One licence, one medical visit: a single check confirms all the categories on it.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'due specifiche visite mediche': one visit is enough.

sceneParams.caption: A and B together: one medical visit

q24691.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, lasts eight years if issued or confirmed to someone aged between 50 and 70.

explain.short: From 50 to 70 licence B lasts 5 years, not 8.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'otto anni': wrong number; it is 5.

q24692.en: A category BE licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, lasts five years if issued or confirmed to someone who is not over 50.

explain.short: BE follows B: under 50 it lasts 10 years, not 5.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'cinque anni' with 'non ha superato i 50 anni': wrong, it is 10.

q24693.en: A category B licence cannot be renewed for someone who is over 80.

explain.short: There is no age limit for licence B. Over 80 it is renewed every 2 years after a medical check.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'non può essere rinnovata': wrong, it can, every 2 years.

q24694.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, lasts five years if issued or confirmed to someone who is not over 50.

explain.short: Under 50 licence B lasts 10 years. 5 years is for the 50 to 70 age range.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'cinque anni' with 'non ha superato i 50 anni': wrong, it is 10.

q24695.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it or the date is aligned to the holder's birthday, lasts ten years in every case of issue or confirmation.

explain.short: 10 years is only for drivers up to 50. After that the periods get shorter: 5, 3, then 2 years.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case): wrong, it depends on age.

q24696.en: A category B licence, unless a different limit is written on it, has no expiry date until the holder turns 50.

explain.short: Every licence has an expiry date. Under 50 it lasts 10 years, then it must be renewed.
explain.rule: The licence is confirmed after a medical check by an authorised doctor (physical and mental fitness). B, BE and A: 10 years under 50, 5 years from 50 to 70, 3 years from 70 to 80, 2 years over 80. An expired licence cannot be used.
explain.trap: 'non ha scadenza di validità': wrong, it always expires.
